entries.topic: The security zone, the SLA, Khiam, the Amal-Hezbollah war, Taif, Musawi and Nasrallah, 1985-1992

claims.text: The Israeli-occupied zone covered about 850 sq km (332 sq mi), roughly 10% of Lebanon, with about 150,000 residents in 162 villages and towns; SLA 2,500-3,000 men alongside 1,000-1,200 IDF troops

Israel helped establish the SLA's predecessor under Sa'ad Haddad in 1976 and supplied advisers and materiel; ex-IDF general Avraham Tamir: 'huge sums of money were invested in fortifying and equipping the SLA'; Antoine Lahd headed the SLA from 1985

CRS: Israel established the SLA in 1985 as 'an allied militia that it fully funded and equipped'; paid members about $500-800 a month; annual cost estimated at $35 million; zone about nine miles deep; reported composition ~30% Shia, 13% Druze, 7% Sunni, rest Christian (some say Shia up to half)
CRS: roughly 250 IDF fatalities 1985-April 2000 (Reuters); SLA spokesman: 621 military and 200 civilian SLA fatalities to March 2000

Haddad proclaimed the 'State of Free Lebanon' in April 1979 from Metulla; force renamed South Lebanon Army May 1980; Haddad died January 1984 and Lahd took over April 1984; Shia became the majority partly because salaries attracted recruits

Israel's defense ministry told the High Court in a September 1999 affidavit that Khiam was 'under the responsibility' of the SLA and its staff were Lebanese, but admitted Shin Bet personnel met SLA interrogators several times a year and 'cooperate with members of the SLA, and even assist them by means of professional guidance and training', and consulted on arrests and releases; HRW said Israel, as occupying power, bore ultimate responsibility; 141 held without charge

Amnesty 1992: about 200 detainees at Khiam, held without legal basis, no ICRC access ever permitted, no family contact since 1988; evidence 'suggests that Israeli officials have been directly involved' in interrogation and torture, at least until 1988

Shin Bet documents released after a High Court petition by lawyer Eitay Mack: a 1987 Shin Bet report said the SLA ran Khiam with personnel trained by the IDF and Shin Bet, detainees were held without charge or detention orders for indefinite periods; 250-300 held at any time
Amal-Hezbollah 'War of Brothers' April 1988-November 1990; Damascus Agreement 30 January 1989 brokered by Syria's al-Sharaa and Iran's Velayati; casualty estimates vary widely

Taif signed 22 October 1989, ratified 5 November 1989; required disarmament of all militias; deadline set 30 April 1991; Hezbollah allowed to remain armed as a 'resistance force' against Israel's occupation of the south

In 1991 Amal gave its weapons to the Lebanese army, the PSP to the Syrian army, the Lebanese Forces part of its arsenal; 'Hezbollah, however, neither surrendered its weapons nor entered any discussions on disarmament'
Israeli helicopters killed Abbas al-Musawi with his wife, five-year-old son and others on 16 February 1992; Bergman/Bednarz reported an original abduction plan; Hassan Nasrallah succeeded him
Hezbollah entered parliament for the first time in the August 1992 elections, winning 'a landslide' in eastern Lebanon

entries.topic: Operation Accountability 1993, Grapes of Wrath and Qana 1996, the April Understanding, Hezbollah rocket fire

claims.text: Operation Accountability: about 120 Lebanese civilians killed, close to 500 injured, some 300,000 displaced; 2 Israeli civilians killed and 24 injured by Hezbollah rockets; informal US-brokered July understanding took effect 31 July 1993

Rabin to the Knesset, 28 July 1993: goal to 'restore security to the lives of residents in communities of the north'; aim to move Lebanese civilians north and pressure Lebanon and Syria to restrain Hezbollah; cited 92 IDF soldiers and civilians killed since the zone was created
Accountability: 25-31 July 1993; IDF artillery fired about 25,000 rounds; about 150 rockets fired into northern Israel; preceded by July clashes in which Israeli soldiers were killed

HRW: an unnamed Israeli official told the Wall Street Journal in April 1996 that the policy was to force out civilians to pressure Lebanon; Gen. Yehosh Dorfman 1993: aim 'to destroy the villages and the houses of the activists'

HRW: in 1995 Katyusha attacks caused two civilian deaths and 31 injuries in Israel; Naim Qassem April 1995: 'whenever the Israeli enemy shells and harms civilians in our villages, we will shell northern Palestine'

UN report (van Kappen, 1 May 1996): 'an estimated 100 persons were killed'; 'it is unlikely that the shelling of the United Nations compound was the result of gross technical and/or procedural errors', though this 'cannot be ruled out completely'; mortar fire from 220 m south-west about 15 minutes before; RPV present (Israel said sent after); almost all proximity fuses over the compound
Israel: 'a sequence of operational mistakes and technical failures, compounded by chance'; 'not Israeli policy to target civilians or the United Nations'
Peres: 'We did not know that several hundred people were concentrated in that camp'; Hezbollah 'used the U.N. as a shield'; Shahak: 'I don't see any mistake in judgment'

HRW 1997: Lebanese military reported 154 civilians killed and 351 injured in Grapes of Wrath; UN estimated at least 400,000 displaced; Qana barrage at minimum 'a reckless and negligent attack'; UNIFIL counted ~270 firing incidents at or near UN positions, ~15 by Lebanese guerrillas
US Army article (2016) gives 106 killed at Qana and argues the deaths resulted from fire-direction and map errors, not intent

April Understanding (26 April 1996): armed groups in Lebanon will not attack Israel; Israel and those cooperating with it will not fire at civilians or civilian targets in Lebanon; civilians never targeted, populated areas not used as launch sites; self-defence preserved; Monitoring Group of US, France, Syria, Lebanon and Israel
UN General Assembly drafts repeatedly required Israel to pay some $1.12 million for the Qana incident; Israel had not responded to the request

entries.topic: Withdrawal of May 2000, SLA collapse, Blue Line, Shebaa Farms, October 2000 capture

claims.text: Barak ordered the withdrawal on 23 May 2000 and it was completed the next day; about 1,500 SLA members fled to Israel (6,420-7,000 with dependants); Lebanese army held 1,488; Beirut military tribunal convicted 77 on 5 June with sentences of one month to five years

MERIP: last Israeli soldier left early on 24 May 2000, weeks ahead of Barak's 7 July date; withdrawal 'crammed into a chaotic 48 hours'; villagers broke open Khiam's cells; Nasrallah said withdrawal not complete until Shebaa Farms liberated and detainees released
Four Mothers movement began 1997 after 73 soldiers died in a helicopter accident; Barak pledged to 'bring the boys home' by July 2000
Israel Hayom: Israel 'lost 414 soldiers' in its south Lebanon presence (window not stated)

Shebaa Farms: ~25 sq km; SG report S/2000/460 (22 May 2000) used the UNIFIL-UNDOF line, placing the farms in Syrian Golan under resolutions 242/338; Council endorsed 23 May 2000; SG confirmed compliance with 425 on 16 June 2000; Blue Line without prejudice to a future border agreement; Lebanon claims the farms, Syria supports the claim; Israel says they are Syrian Golan; US took no position on sovereignty

On 7 October 2000 Hezbollah seized three Israeli soldiers near the Shebaa Farms (Adi Avitan, Benyamin Avraham, Omar Sawaid); IDF later assessed they were killed during or right after the attack; in the January 2004 exchange Israel released 435 prisoners plus remains of 59 Lebanese for Elchanan Tenenbaum and the soldiers' remains
About 7,500 former SLA members and families live in Israel; a 2011 Lebanese law to regularise their status never got implementing decrees, largely due to Hezbollah's opposition

entries.topic: Buenos Aires 1992 and 1994, Nisman, Burgas 2012, EU listing 2013

claims.text: Israeli embassy in Buenos Aires bombed 17 March 1992; usually counted 29 dead (a 1999 Supreme Court act set its own figure at 22), 200+ injured; Supreme Court found on 10 May 1999 the attack was organised and carried out by Islamic Jihad and later named Imad Mughniyah; a claim signed 'Islamic Jihad Organization' was sent to An-Nahar
The Islamic Jihad claim said the embassy attack avenged Musawi's son

Federal Criminal Cassation Court (Mahiques, Ledesma, Barroetaveña), 11 April 2024, 711 pages: Iran ordered both the 1992 embassy and 1994 AMIA attacks; Hezbollah carried them out under 'the inspiration, organisation, planning and financing of state and parastatal bodies subordinate to the Ayatollahs' government'; both crimes against humanity; motive revenge for Argentina's cancellation of three nuclear contracts; Galeano's cover-up sentence reduced; Menem acquitted; no one ever arrested
AMIA bombing 18 July 1994 killed 85, about 300 injured; court called Iran a 'terrorist state'; judge Mahiques: attack carried out 'under the mandate of a government, of a State'
Prosecutors in October 2006 accused Iran and Hezbollah, seeking arrest of Rafsanjani, six other officials and Imad Mughniyeh; Iran's foreign ministry called it 'Zionist propaganda'
Hezbollah rejected Argentine claims that it carried out the AMIA bombing, saying the named bomber had been killed fighting Israel in south Lebanon

Nisman found dead 18 January 2015 hours before presenting evidence that Kirchner covered up Iran's role; judge Ercolini ruled December 2017 his death 'could not have been a suicide'; Kirchner called the case an 'absurdity'

Judge Rafecas ordered trial in absentia (June 2025) of ten Iranian and Lebanese suspects including Fallahian, Velayati, Rezai, Vahidi, under a March 2025 law; Iran denies involvement and refuses extradition
Cassation Court in September 2026 declared trial in absentia constitutional, clearing the way to an oral trial; no trial date reported

Burgas 18 July 2012: five Israeli tourists and a Bulgarian driver killed; bomber Mohamad Hassan El Husseini; Specialised Criminal Court in September 2020 sentenced Meliad Farah and Hassan El Hajj Hassan in absentia to life for logistical support; Hezbollah denies involvement
Tsvetanov, 5 February 2013: 'A reasonable assumption can be made that the two of them were members of the militant wing of Hezbollah'
In June 2013 FM Vigenin said there was 'no conclusive evidence'; in July 2013 interior minister Yovchev said 'clear signs'; Netanyahu immediately blamed Hezbollah and Iran; Iran called it 'baseless'

EU foreign ministers on 22 July 2013 listed Hezbollah's military wing, citing Burgas and a Cyprus conviction; Ashton: does not prevent 'dialogue with all political parties in Lebanon'; Qassem (Oct 2012): 'We don't have a military wing and a political one'
